divergence.label: Dispatch note and permit agree on product but name different tanks. The operator matches on product, not on tank
Local handle left in hand after the last job, so the start from the control room does nothing
Started P-202, the pump for the other rack, because the panel tag moved when the panel was replaced
Started the pump with the inlet still shut, which is the definition of a dead-headed line
The vent was shut for the roof inspection. It is up the platform ladder, off the transfer walk, and nobody thought of it
Opened the nitrogen blanket valve next to the vent. The tank now pressurises instead of breathing, which looks like a healthy result on the status board
Climbed the ladder, found the handle stiff, forced it a quarter turn and assumed it was through
Level rising slower than the estimate, so he opened the recirculation bypass to keep the pump loaded, against step 13
Closed V1 before stopping the pump, so the trapped column hammered and the couplings wept
Went back to the rack office to close the permit paperwork, and the level crossed while he was typing
The local indicator has been reading low since the transmitter bench test. He stops the pump when it says 9.30 and the tank is already above it
Left the watch entirely to help the other bay discharge a late load
Broke the coupling before the line had drained, so the contents of the hose went on the deck
Opened V2, the draw-off valve on the same manifold with the same handwheel and a tag nobody can read from the working platform
Closed by hand but the stem packing is stiff and the disc is two turns off its seat
The meter is a cumulative total, not a batch total. He works the difference out from memory
Already stopped on level, so he does not look at the meter again
Permit signed in the office against yesterday's load; the tank named on it is TK-103
No permit at all, because it is the fourth load of the week into the same tank
The register is in the control room and the shift is behind. Assumed the fitter signed it back like he always does
Confirmed the row for LT-101. The isolation that matters is the next row down, LSHH-101
Transmitter confirmed in service. Nobody looked at whether the high-high switch loop was proved after the bench test
Bond clip is on the painted chassis rail. It looks connected and measures nothing
Walked past it because the driver said he had just made up for the last load
Checked the bond on the vehicle in the adjacent bay
Assumed V1 had been left open from the last transfer into this tank
Cracked the cross-connect V3 open to free a stuck stem, and left it there
Rising stem valve turned the wrong way: the handwheel came up, which reads as open
Knew V2 was closed because he closed it himself at the end of the last transfer
The valve is quarter-turn and the indicator plate was refitted upside down after the packing change
V3 is only used for tank cleaning, so it never occurs to him as something to check
Did the walk from the rack only as far as the first bend, where the manifold is out of sight
Confirmed the valves visible from the walkway, which does not include the tank bottom outlet
Walked the line while talking on the radio about the next load, and registered the positions he expected rather than the ones he passed
Cleared the tray by pushing last shift's standing liquid over the weep hole into the bund drain, so the tray is empty for this transfer and the bund is not
Tray looked dry from above
Read the gauge board of the tank two bays along, which sits at a similar height
No start level written down, so the delivered quantity has to be judged by eye later
The totaliser on the adjacent rack is at a similar number and is the one visible from the road
Pump stopped at the handle but not isolated. The next crew will find it running against a closed inlet
Closed V3 instead of V1, leaving the inlet open to a tank that is no longer receiving
Left the hose in the tray, dripping
Written up next shift from memory, so a wrong-tank receipt stays invisible until the monthly stock reconciliation
Logged the indicated level as the true level, carrying the instrument error into the stock record
Status board left showing TK-101 as not receiving, so the next dispatch is planned into a full tank
Release not noticed, or noticed and not believed
